crypt-01-c1.text: Andrey Bogdanov, Dmitry Khovratovich, Christian Rechberger (2011). Biclique Cryptanalysis of the Full AES. ASIACRYPT 2011 (Cryptology ePrint Archive 2011/449).
crypt-01-c1.quote: The first key recovery attack on the full AES-128 with computational complexity 2126.1.
crypt-01-c1.claim: The best known attack on AES-128 (biclique, 2011) reduces complexity to 2^126.1, barely better than brute force.

crypt-01-c3.text: Hanno Böck, Aaron Zauner, Sean Devlin, Juraj Somorovsky, Philipp Jovanovic (2016). Nonce-Disrespecting Adversaries: Practical Forgery Attacks on GCM in TLS. 10th USENIX Workshop on Offensive Technologies (WOOT 16).
crypt-01-c3.quote: With an Internet-wide scan we identified 184 HTTPS servers repeating nonces, which fully breaks the authenticity of the connections.
crypt-01-c3.claim: A 2016 study (Böck et al.) found TLS servers on the internet that actually repeated GCM nonces, plus tens of thousands more that used random nonces and were at risk of collision.

crypt-01-c3.text: E. Rescorla (IETF) (2018). RFC 8446: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3. RFC Editor / IETF.
crypt-01-c3.quote: A TLS-compliant application MUST implement the TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 [GCM] cipher suite and SHOULD implement the TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 [GCM] and TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256 [RFC8439] cipher suites
crypt-01-c3.claim: In TLS 1.3, AES-128-GCM is mandatory to implement and ChaCha20-Poly1305 is recommended.

crypt-02-c3.text: David Adrian, Karthikeyan Bhargavan, Zakir Durumeric, Pierrick Gaudry, Matthew Green, J. Alex Halderman, Nadia Heninger, Drew Springall, Emmanuel Thomé, Luke Valenta, Benjamin VanderSloot, Eric Wustrow, Santiago Zanella-Béguelin, Paul Zimmermann (2015). Imperfect Forward Secrecy: How Diffie-Hellman Fails in Practice. weakdh.org / 22nd ACM CCS.
crypt-02-c3.quote: We further estimate that an academic team can break a 768-bit prime and that a nation-state can break a 1024-bit prime.
crypt-02-c3.claim: The 2015 Logjam paper showed that nation-state attackers could plausibly precompute against the small set of 1024-bit primes hardcoded into every major TLS server, then break individual sessions cheaply.

crypt-04-c1.text: Marc Stevens, Elie Bursztein, Pierre Karpman, Ange Albertini, Yarik Markov (2017). SHAttered. shattered.io (CWI Amsterdam and Google).
crypt-04-c1.quote: showed the world the first real collision for the SHA-1 hash function
crypt-04-c1.claim: SHA-1 (160-bit) was broken in 2017 with the SHAttered collision

crypt-05-c2.claim: Argon2 won the Password Hashing Competition (2015)
